title: Grant of Deemed University Status to NCERT
body_text:
The application of National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT),  New Delhi for grant of Institution Deemed to be University status was examined by the  University Grant Commission (UGC) through its Expert Committee as per the provisions of  the UGC (Institutions Deemed to be Universities) Regulations, 2023. The Committee, after  overall assessment, recommended for grant of Institutions Deemed to be University to NCERT,  New Delhi. Considering the advice of UGC, the Ministry of Education, vide Notification dated  30.03.2026, declared NCERT, New Delhi as an Institution Deemed to be University under  Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956. The said declaration was subject to condition that it shall take  appropriate steps to commence research programmes as well as doctoral and innovative  academic programmes.
The status of Institution Deemed to be University will strengthen the NCERT to promote  educational research & innovation and collaborate with national and international agencies. It  will further reinforce its role as a think tank and as national resource institution engaged in  providing technical support to the Central Government as well as State Governments.
This information was given by the Minister of State for Education, DR. Sukanta Majumdar, in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.
*****
RRTN

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Education informed Lok Sabha that NCERT, New Delhi has been declared an Institution Deemed to be University under Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956, via a notification dated 30.03.2026. This followed a recommendation by a UGC Expert Committee under the UGC (Institutions Deemed to be Universities) Regulations, 2023, with the condition that NCERT initiate research, doctoral, and innovative academic programmes.
enrichment.context:
NCERT is India's apex body for school education, responsible for developing the National Curriculum Framework, textbooks, and teacher training modules, and for advising central and state governments on pedagogy and curriculum policy. Deemed University status, granted under Section 3 of the UGC Act 1956, allows institutions with a strong record of specialized work to award their own degrees and design autonomous academic programmes without affiliating to an existing university. For NCERT, this status is significant because it will now be able to offer doctoral (PhD) and other higher academic programmes directly, deepening its research capacity in educational studies rather than functioning solely as a curriculum and resource body.

This move is consistent with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020's emphasis on strengthening teacher education and educational research institutions, and integrating research into mainstream academic institutions. It also reflects a broader trend of premier national institutes—like IITs and ICAR institutes—seeking deemed university status to enhance academic autonomy and global collaboration. The condition attached (mandatory research and doctoral programmes) ensures accountability, aligning with UGC's 2023 Regulations that tightened oversight of deemed universities following past concerns over quality dilution.

prelims_questions.question: Under which section of the UGC Act, 1956 is 'Institution Deemed to be University' status granted?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states NCERT was declared a Deemed University 'under Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956', which is the standard provision governing deemed university status.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following statements about NCERT is correct?
options: It was established under the UGC Act, 1956
It has been granted Institution Deemed to be University status in 2026
It is a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament
It only functions at the state level
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, the Ministry of Education declared NCERT an Institution Deemed to be University via notification dated 30.03.2026; NCERT itself is a registered society, not a statutory body under UGC Act.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of granting 'Institution Deemed to be University' status to bodies like NCERT in strengthening India's educational research ecosystem, in light of the National Education Policy 2020.
Examine the role of the University Grants Commission in regulating deemed universities in India. What safeguards exist to ensure quality after such status is granted?
